reader_question: How do I ask a federal agency for its records, and what can I do if it says no?
grade_line: Documented: the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. 552, as in force on November 12, 2026
title: A federal agency has 20 working days under the law to answer a records request, and a requester it turns down can appeal, ask for mediation or sue.
measure_line: What a requester does to get records from a federal agency under 5 U.S.C. 552, in order, with the longest time the law allows at each step
notes: Federal agencies take weeks or months to answer requests for public records, as our systems atlas records in Issue I013 “Public records arrive too late to be useful”.
The steps cover federal agencies only; each state has its own public records law.
alt: Eight steps a requester takes to get records from a federal agency, two of them optional, each with the time the law allows.

table.caption: Requesting records from a federal agency, step by step

branches.4: Optional, when the need is urgent
branches.7: Optional, in place of a lawsuit
